title: RAW f69r compass orientation from an independently identified east-west event
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED. Seek an already admitted, visually owned solar rising/setting or equivalent east-west event whose direction can be established without Voynich words or f69r geometry. Only if such an anchor and a demonstrable orientation link to f69r both exist, freeze its bearing before reading the 16 f69r sectors and test complete labels against independently owned directional material. If either link is missing, stop; the existing 180-degree wind-source versus destination ambiguity remains.

design.mechanism: An external east-west event plus a manuscript-internal frame relation could orient a wind rose without choosing a wind name from its own circular geometry.
design.unit: One independently identified east-west visual event, its validated frame link to f69r, all 16 complete f69r outer sectors, and an independently owned directional comparator if available.
design.contrast: Anchor-fixed east-west alignment versus the 180-degree partner and other rotation/reflection alignments; whole-label semantic predictions versus generic cyclic structure.
design.prediction: A genuinely bound east-west event selects a unique f69r orientation before its text is read; if a separate direction-owned text comparator exists, the frozen mapping makes different complete-sector predictions for at least one candidate reading. No unique anchor or comparator means no semantic score.
design.scope: Only already admitted visual and text selectors; f84/f84r and reserved material closed. No inherited word gloss or component rule. Historical visual analogy alone is insufficient; the east-west event and frame transfer require independent evidence.
